plan.contextChunk: This figure is part of a worked example asking to evaluate the polar double integral of sin theta over the region R in the first quadrant outside the circle r = 2 and inside the cardioid r = 2(1 + cos theta). The figure shows both curves in polar coordinates: the circle r = 2 (blue) centered at the origin and the cardioid r = 2(1 + cos theta) (purple), which extends further to the right. The shaded region R (light blue) lies in the first quadrant between theta = 0 and theta = pi/2, bounded on the inside by the circle and on the outside by the cardioid; a red radial line at an intermediate angle shows a representative radial strip. The figure establishes the geometry of the integration region R needed to set up the polar iterated integral with inner limits from r = 2 to r = 2(1 + cos theta) and outer limits from theta = 0 to theta = pi/2.

interactionPlan.concept: Polar double integrals are constructed by sweeping a radial ray over an angular range, with the inner and outer limits defined by the radial distance to each bounding curve.
elements: Horizontal (x) and vertical (y) axes crossing at the origin
Blue circular path representing r = 2, centered at the origin
Purple cardioid path representing r = 2(1 + cos(theta))
Light blue shaded region in the first quadrant bounded between the blue circle (inner) and purple cardioid (outer)
Red radial line segment originating at the origin and terminating on the outer boundary at a specific angle theta
Text labels: 'r = 2' (near the circle), 'r = 2(1 + cos θ)' (near the cardioid), 'θ = π/2' (on the positive y-axis), and 'θ = 0' (on the positive x-axis)

interactions.label: Outer Boundary
interactions.teaches: The shape of the integration region and its upper intersection limit are determined directly by the formula for the outer boundary curve.

interactions.label: Radial sweep (θ)
interactions.teaches: Sweeping the angle visualizes the continuous integration over theta, showing how each radial slice is bounded by the inner and outer curves.

demo_steps.title: Region Boundaries
demo_steps.narration: The region of integration is bounded below by theta = 0, above by theta = pi/2, inside by the circle r = 2, and outside by the cardioid.

demo_steps.title: Radial Slices
demo_steps.narration: Sweep the slider to move the red radial strip. Notice that at any angle theta, the shaded segment of the ray starts precisely at r = 2 and ends at r = 2(1+cos(theta)), defining the limits for the inner integral.

demo_steps.title: Modify the Outer Curve
demo_steps.narration: Try changing the equation of the outer boundary (for instance, to 3). The outer curve updates, reshaping the shaded integration region and moving the intersection point where the inner and outer bounds meet.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: In a polar double integral, the inner integration limits are simply the distances along a radial ray from the origin to the inner and outer boundary curves.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Maintain aspect ratio 1:1 so the circle is perfectly round. Circle path should be a clean, solid blue line. Cardioid path should be a solid purple line. The light blue region must precisely fill the area between the two curves in the first quadrant. The red line must originate at (0,0) and end on the path defined by the equation_input. Label text should be italicized with standard math formatting.
